GOP Rep. Tom Kean Jr. took four months off from Congress, fully paid, to treat depression. Time and again, he’s voted against paid sick leave legislation.

U.S. Rep. Tom Kean Jr. (R-N.J.) just took a taxpayer-funded four-month absence from Congress to treat clinical depression — despite repeatedly voting against paid sick leave for workers while serving as a State Senator in New Jersey.

Kean opposed a 2018 New Jersey law requiring employers to provide up to 40 hours of paid time off for workers dealing with an illness or a medical condition. In 2008, Kean similarly voted against legislation that extended paid parental and family leave benefits to workers for up to six weeks through a state insurance program.

The Lever followed the money behind the architect of the conservative supermajority on the Supreme Court, Leonard Leo — and uncovered that his operation had been supercharged by a record-breaking $1.6 billion secret tax-free donation from Chicago businessman Barre Seid.

In the aftermath, President Biden highlighted the donation in a major speech urging Congress to pass a bill getting dark money out of politics.

In April 2025, The Lever released its investigation into how several firms in the tax industry donated more than $137,000 to Trump’s nominee to lead the IRS—which conveniently absolved him of virtually that exact amount of debt from a failed 2022 senate race.

The next month, a group of senators released a letter demanding more information about the donations, repeatedly citing The Lever’s original reporting in their demands.
